t.7.66.1: Having heard those words of Nārada, which were like nectar, he obtained incomparable joy and spoke this to Lakṣmaṇa.
t.7.66.2: Go, gentle Lakṣmaṇa, and console that best of the twice-born; and have the boy's body placed in a vat of oil.
t.7.66.3: With the finest perfumes and richly fragrant oils, gentle one, let it be arranged so that the boy's body does not decay.
t.7.66.5: Having thus instructed Lakṣmaṇa of auspicious marks, the greatly renowned Kākutstha thought of the Puṣpaka in his mind, saying, "Come!"
t.7.66.4: Act in such a way that neither decay nor disintegration may befall the body of the boy of untainted deeds, who is being kept under protection.
t.7.66.6: Understanding his intention, the gold-adorned Puṣpaka came in a moment into the presence of Rāghava.
t.7.66.8: Having heard the pleasing words of Puṣpaka, the lord of men saluted those great sages and then mounted the aerial chariot.
t.7.66.7: Having bowed low, he said: "Here I am, O lord of men, obedient to you, O mighty-armed one; I have come before you as your servant."
t.7.66.10: He went to the west, searching the deserts on every side, and then the glorious one went to the northern quarter, enclosed by the Himālaya.
t.7.66.9: Taking up his bow, his quiver, and his sword of brilliant splendor, and leaving both heroes, Saumitri and Bharata, behind in the city.
t.7.66.11: Seeing not even the slightest wrongdoing there either, the lord of men then surveyed the entire eastern region as well.
t.7.66.12: Then the son of the royal sage went toward the southern direction, and on the northern side of Śaivala he saw a very great lake.
t.7.66.13: At that lake the illustrious Rāghava saw an ascetic practicing very great austerity, hanging with his face turned downward.
t.7.66.14: Then, approaching him as he practised the supreme austerity, Rāghava spoke these words: "Blessed are you, O you of excellent vows."
t.7.66.15: In what birth do you abide, O you who have grown great in austerity, O you of firm valor? I ask you out of curiosity, for I am Rāma, the son of Daśaratha.
t.7.66.16: What, pray, is the aim you have set your heart on: the attainment of heaven, or something resting on a boon, relying on which you have performed this austerity? I wish to hear it, O ascetic.
t.7.66.17: Are you a brāhmaṇa, blessings be upon you, or are you an invincible kṣatriya? Or are you a vaiśya, or else a śūdra? Tell me this truthfully.
